subject: Culture
title: Caste and Class Lines
description: A fast breakdown of Caste and Class Lines for builders.

hook.text: India's caste system is over 3,000 years old. It was outlawed in 1950 but never really vanished.

buildup.text: Caste determined your job, marriage, and meals. Crossing lines meant exile from your community.

discovery.text: Britain's class system works similarly—accent, school, and postcode signal your rank instantly.

twist.text: American culture claims to be classless, but zip code predicts life expectancy better than genetics.

climax.text: Every society sorts people. The labels change but the sorting never stops.

punchline.text: Hierarchy hides behind different names everywhere.

quiz.question: When was caste-based discrimination officially outlawed in India?

details.summary: Caste systems create invisible boundaries that taboo contact between social groups. India's caste system forbade inter-caste dining, marriage, and even proximity for millennia.
details.whyItMatters: Caste taboos persist even where legally abolished, affecting billions. Understanding these invisible social walls is essential for grasping global inequality.
takeaways: India's caste system organized society into hereditary occupational groups
Untouchability was legally abolished in 1950 but persists socially
Caste-like systems exist in Japan, West Africa, and elsewhere

faq.question: How does the Indian caste system work?
faq.answer: The system divides Hindus into four varnas (Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, Shudras) with Dalits ('untouchables') outside this hierarchy. Caste is determined by birth and traditionally governed occupation, marriage, and social interaction.

faq.question: Do caste-like systems exist outside India?
faq.answer: Yes. Japan's burakumin are descendants of a feudal outcast class who still face discrimination. West African griot lineages and blacksmith castes have hereditary status. Yemen's akhdam caste faces severe discrimination.
